archetype.name: Game Manager (quick-game backup)
archetype.definition: A low-aDOT, rhythm-throw backup who can keep a good offense on schedule when protected, but gives back his gains when he has to push the ball past the sticks or play off-script.

report.headline: Steady underneath, costly past ten yards: a backup who needs clean pockets
report.take:
Tyson Bagent is back to QB2 behind Caleb Williams after a three-week stretch in which he took real snaps: a cameo against Minnesota, a full game against the Jets and a start at Green Bay. Three games and 64 attempts are thin, but the profile matches his 2023 rookie season closely. His EPA per dropback was -0.093 then and is -0.077 now. His completion rate sat at 65.7% then and 65.6% now. He was a below-average passer who completes a good share of what he throws. The style hasn't changed either: intended air yards of 6.02, air yards to the sticks at -1.93, and the ball out in 2.84 seconds.

The season splits cleanly by depth. Under ten air yards he has been useful: short throws (0-9) produce +0.23 EPA with a 62.1% success rate and a +5.6 CPOE across 29 attempts. That is the Ben Johnson offense working as designed, with a backup quarterback simply delivering on time. From 10 to 19 yards the picture flips. He is 41.2% with a -13.8 CPOE, and all three of his interceptions came on those 17 throws. The handful of deep shots went well (+0.774 EPA on 5 attempts), but that is too few plays to mean much.

The two meaningful games show how far apart his floor and ceiling are. Against the Jets he was pressured on just 5.6% of dropbacks and posted +7.9 EPA on 268 yards. At Green Bay, in his lone official start, he was pressured more and threw poorly. His bad-throw rate there was 23.8%, his CPOE was -10.9, he threw two interceptions, and his passing EPA was -10.3 in a 31-7 loss. That gap tracks how much stress the defense put on him. His pressure-to-sack rate (40%, 35th of 38) also clashes with his 2023 mark (19.2%, 4th of 66). With only four sacks in that number, treat it as noise more than a new flaw.

The zero touchdowns stand out (tdPct 44th of 45), and some of it is variance on low volume. Some of it is real, though: in the red zone he is 46.7% with -0.339 EPA a play, and the compressed field takes away the space his quick game lives on. For the rest of the season he is insurance. He looks like a competent fill-in for a good scheme against average defenses, and a liability against fronts that can heat him up and sit on underneath routes.

strengths.title: Accurate, on-time underneath passing
strengths.body: His short throws are the one area that consistently adds value: +0.23 EPA a play, 72.4% completions and a +5.6 CPOE. That comes from quick decisions in a well-schemed offense rather than arm talent. It matches the high success rate he had as a rookie, so it should hold whenever he plays.

strengths.title: Functional when kept clean
strengths.body: In the Jets game the line kept pressure to 5.6% of his dropbacks. He went 25/34 for 268 yards and +7.9 EPA, the only game he has played with a positive result. The offense around him ranks 10th in pass EPA, so a protected Bagent can borrow a lot from the scheme.

strengths.title: Connection with Odunze
strengths.body: Rome Odunze has turned his 12 targets into +0.587 EPA each, by far the best of any receiver Bagent has thrown to. It is a small sample, but it gives him a reliable outside answer if he is forced into action.

concerns.title: Intermediate throws are turnovers waiting
concerns.body: All three of his interceptions came on 17 throws between 10 and 19 air yards, where his CPOE is -13.8. This is where a backup's limits in processing and velocity show up against zone defenders. It also matches his 2023 line of 6 interceptions in 5 games, so it looks like part of who he is rather than bad luck.

concerns.title: Falls apart under stress
concerns.body: At Green Bay his bad-throw rate jumped to 23.8% and his EPA per dropback as a starter was -0.448. Under center he has managed -0.285 EPA a play, compared with roughly break-even from shotgun. When the defense dictates terms or the play needs more than a quick read, his accuracy goes.

concerns.title: Red zone and the Loveland disconnect
concerns.body: He has no touchdowns on 64 attempts. In the red zone he completes under half his throws, at -0.339 EPA a play. His 14 targets to Colston Loveland have cost -0.588 EPA each, which matters more with Cole Kmet now on IR and Loveland the only real tight end. Some of this will even out, but a compressed field takes away his strength.

trend.note: His passing EPA swung from -2.8 in a relief cameo to +7.9 against the Jets to -10.3 at Green Bay, then Williams reclaimed the job in Week 6. There is no trend to follow while he sits on the bench.

nextGame.headline: Inactive role likely; Seattle's defense would punish any relief appearance
nextGame.body:
Bagent is the QB2 behind a healthy Williams, so the most likely outcome in Seattle is no snaps at all. If he did come in, this is about the worst matchup for his profile. Seattle ranks 2nd in defensive EPA, 3rd against the pass and 3rd in hit rate, and gives up the fewest explosive passes in the league. The only soft spot is short passing, where Seattle sits 21st in EPA allowed. That is exactly where he lives, but a defense that hits quarterbacks this often would put him in the pressure situations that sank him at Green Bay.

On Chicago's side, Kmet on IR leaves Loveland as the primary tight end, and Bagent has struggled to connect with him. Monangai being out thins the backfield behind D'Andre Swift. Seattle's notable absences are linebacker Drake Thomas, an 87% snap player, which loosens the middle of the field, and tackle Charles Cross on their offense, which helps Chicago's pass rush more than Bagent himself.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game against a soft underneath zone
keyMatchups.body: Seattle allows +0.117 EPA on short passes while shutting down everything deep. A backup who throws short would be playing into the defense's one weakness, especially with Drake Thomas out at linebacker.

keyMatchups.title: Seattle pressure against his pocket
keyMatchups.body: Seattle ranks 3rd in hit rate. Bagent's worst game came when the pocket wasn't clean, and his sack rate under pressure this year is near the bottom of the league.

nextGame.watch: Whether Williams takes every snap. Bagent only matters here if he doesn't.

restOfSeason.body:
As QB2 he projects to near-zero usage unless Williams misses time. The ranges below are what to expect in any game he starts. He is a game manager who can borrow from a top-ten passing offense against middling defenses, as the Jets game showed. Expect the short-game efficiency to hold and the touchdown drought to break with more volume. The intermediate interceptions and pressure-driven collapses look like part of who he is, given how closely this season tracks 2023.

In a start, think roughly 150-230 passing yards, about one touchdown at most, and close to an interception a game. The outcome depends on the opponent's pass rush far more than on anything he does differently.
swingFactors: Quality of the opposing pass rush
Loveland's role with Kmet on IR

confidence.note: 64 attempts across three games, and he is currently a backup with no defined role.
